name: Dapagliflozin
mechanism: Promotes glucosuria by inhibiting renal SGLT2
contraindications: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (risk of DKA), severe renal impairment or dialysis (reduced efficacy), pregnancy and breastfeeding; avoid if eGFR below licensed threshold
interactions: Concomitant diuretics may increase risk of volume depletion and hypotension; insulin or insulin secretagogues increase hypoglycaemia risk — dose adjustments may be required
monitoring: Assess renal function before initiation and periodically; monitor blood pressure, signs of volume depletion, and for genital mycotic infections; enquire about symptoms suggestive of DKA if unwell
pregnancy: Avoid use in pregnancy; discontinue if pregnancy is planned or confirmed and seek specialist advice
sideEffects: Common: genital mycotic infections, polyuria, thirst; less common but serious: volume depletion, rare cases of euglycaemic DKA; monitor accordingly
clinicalPearls: Provides glycaemic control and has demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in specific patient groups; ensure appropriate patient education on genital hygiene and sick-day rules
indication: Type 2 diabetes to improve glycaemic control; also indicated in selected patients for heart failure or chronic kidney disease per guideline recommendations
